reason: All opcodes are real on the 65SC12 (BRA, abs,X/abs,Y LDA/CMP/STA; no Rockwell bit ops). The logic matches: CMP on the high bytes leaves A = the live one's high byte and C/Z for the high bytes, and BNE does not touch C. If the high bytes differ, C=1 keeps the old value and C=0 copies both bytes, as the 16-bit compare did. If they are equal, the low CMP's C decides; on a copy A still holds the live low byte and the high byte is already equal, so memory ends up the same. A and flags are dead at x1_kept (the x2 section starts with LDA). Laid out from &98FD: BNE &9903->&9912, BCS &990B->&991D, BRA &9910->&991D and BCS &9912->&991D all stay inside page &99, so none takes a page-cross penalty.
